Sharpened the sixmax blueprint-vs-PotOdds baseline curve to 20,000 decks/ckpt (120k hands, +/-~50 BB/100 CIs) for all 10 snapshots (this-run increments 100k-1M = 1.1M-2.0M total iters), run 10-way parallel via sixmax/checkpoints/run_curve_20k.sh (~35 min, nohup+caffeinate). Result: curve is CONFIDENTLY FLAT at ~-485 BB/100 with no monotonic trend across iterations. The earlier 3k-deck run's apparent -377/-529 spread was pure variance and collapsed to the mean once CIs tightened 4x. This confirms the documented root cause is training scale, not eval fidelity or a deployment bug: the blueprint loses ~5 BB/hand to a passive baseline because regret-matched policies remain near-uniform over bet sizes at ~16 visits/infoset. Updated sixmax/checkpoints/curve.csv and ROUTER.md project state. So the plateau is not cleanly undertraining vs structural ceiling. Next levers: per-deck paired eval slope (tie-breaker, still unbuilt) + avg-vs-current strategy check at frozen premium nodes. ROOT-CAUSED and FIXED the 6-max blueprint plateau (commit b739363). It was a TRAINER BUG, not undertraining or a coarse abstraction (both earlier hypotheses wrong). Mechanism: BlueprintTrainer + reference MCCFRTrainer dealt a FRESH hand per traverser inside each iteration; new_hand() does button=(button+1)%n, so n deals advanced the button a full cycle per iteration, phase-locking (first_to_act - traverser) to a constant. The traverser was pinned to ONE button-relative seat (empirically after=3), so every other seat's decisions -- including the UTG open where AA/KK first act (after=5) -- accumulated average strategy (huge strategy_sum mass) but EXACTLY-ZERO regret, leaving regret-matching at uniform forever. That is why AA opened identically to 72o and the BB/100 curve was flat at ~-485. Found via the diagnose_blueprint autopsy (frozen probes) + systematic-debugging instrumentation (per-(live,after) regret-vs-mass breakdown showed the after-specific zero-regret pattern, reproduced single-thread). Fix: deal ONE hand per iteration, traverse it once per seat on clones (root=new_hand(); for p: traverse(root->clone(),p)). Applied to both trainers (parity invariant). Regression test_utg_open_decisions_receive_regret asserts the UTG open accrues regret; post-fix the traverser covers all 6 seats (was 1). Both Kuhn -1/18 gates still pass, determinism preserved. CONSEQUENCE: every existing sixmax/checkpoints/*.bin was trained on the broken objective and is INVALID -- retrain from scratch, then re-run eval_sixmax_baseline.py to confirm the curve moves. Corrected the stale 'severe undertraining, not code' claim in ROUTER.md project state.
